messages:
elaine: :rotating_light: FYI — getting several escalations that p95/p99 jumped ~2-3x after last runtime rollout (v2.14.3). Affects text-generation routes (POST /v1/generate). Customers: corpX, storefront-pro. Not seeing rate limit errors, just long tails. Anyone oncall?

sam: looking. canary was at 10% for ~2 hours during the rollout, metrics showed small p50 change but p99 looked fine during canary. I'll pull traces and compare kernels.

raj: I already started digging — noticing a clear change at 15:12:12 UTC (matches rollout). p99 latency spike aligns with a new kernel-selection path: enable_async_kernels=true and kernel-fallback scheduling.

maria: that flag was enabled to prefer newer attention kernels for long sequences. We tested on perf infra but maybe interaction with batching created bad tail behavior. Initial hypothesis: async kernels + large batches -> queueing + hot-path jitter.

nina: Customer repro from corpX (sent by support): small prompt (~80 tokens), concurrency 5, max_tokens 1024, temperature 0.7. They see p95 ~420ms -> p95 ~1.2s after rollout. They included a sample request body and request id: req_8a7f2c.

sam: pulling traces for req_8a7f2c: traceId=abcd-1234-ef. Backend shows heavy wait time in kernel selection and kv-cache attach steps. Stack traces show scheduler wait spikes.

raj: quick checks:
- dashboard: https://dash.redwood/alerts/runtime/p99 (private)
- query I ran: `select percentile(latency_ms, 95), percentile(latency_ms,99) from runtime.requests where model='text-gen' and ts>1954320900`
Output: p95 jumped from ~380ms -> ~1100ms; p99 from ~780ms -> ~2.6s

maria: possible mitigations: 1) revert enable_async_kernels flag (safer), 2) temporarily cap batch_size and batch_timeout to reduce queuing, 3) enable warmup for prefix cache on rollout. We should roll back the kernel selector in prod asap while we bisect.

elaine: agree. Is rollback quick? Any impact on throughput?

raj: rollback is just a config flip in the control plane. Low risk. I'll coordinate a rollback and monitor. Also starting a bisect plan to identify the exact commit/regression window.

maria: for bisect, candidate range: commits from 7a3c9d..d4f21b (kernel selection optimizer + async kernel enable). Steps I'll run locally: 
```
git checkout 7a3c9d
git bisect start d4f21b 7a3c9d
# run perf harness with sample workload
# mark good/bad until we find culprit
```
I will also run a microbench on our perf infra with the customer-like prompt.

deploy-bot: deploy v2.14.3 completed to prod at 1954320895, rollouts: all clusters.

raj: scheduling rollback now — flipping rollout.disable_kernel_selector=true for prod via control plane. Will patch and trigger a canary at 5% then ramp.

sam: also changed batch_policy: `max_batch_tokens=1024` and `max_concurrent_batches=3` in a hotfix for affected pool to minimize queue build-up.

infra-bot: config change applied to pool-03: rollout.disable_kernel_selector=true by raj at 1954321200. Canary -> 5%.

nina: corpX reports initial improvement within ~30s of the canary change; p95 down to ~480ms. They gave fresh request id req_8a7f2d.

maria: running git bisect now on perf harness. Early results: behavior flips between commits d0f9a1 and d3b4c2 — looks like change in scheduler backoff + kernel invocation path.

sam: we should also add a short-term telemetry guard in the control plane: if p99 for a model-route doubles vs baseline in 10m, auto-disable the kernel selector. That could prevent future noisy rollouts.

elaine: good idea. For now, continue rollback and bisect. Raj, keep me posted. We should message customers (corpX + storefront-pro) with an update and ETA.

raj: rollback completed and ramped to 100% at 1954321240. Monitoring now. Current live metrics show p95 back to ~420-520ms and p99 ~760-900ms. Holding for 30m to confirm.

nina: I've sent status updates to both customers with summary and ask for them to reply if they still see issues. :thumbsup:

maria: bisect found the problematic change: commit d1b2f3 introduced an optimization that bypassed a lightweight scheduler backpressure check when async kernels are enabled. Repro steps on perf harness included: 5 concurrent sessions, prompt 70-120 tokens, batch_timeout=25ms.

sam: follow-ups: 1) revert or patch d1b2f3 to restore backpressure check, 2) add a canary metric for kernel latency tail, 3) implement control plane guard (auto-disable). I'll file PRs and link them here.

elaine: thanks everyone. Raj/maria/sam — please post PR links and the postmortem note (short) once bisect + patch are merged. Leaving this thread open until final confirmation after 30m.

raj: confirmed stable at 1954321345. Closing active escalation; will draft postmortem in #postmortems and link customers.
